leadIn:
I’m using the active `settle` workflow: I’ll first trace the export/data-writing flow and its tests, then bring only externally meaningful choices to you through the native question form before changing code.

The initial repository listing is taking longer than expected, so I’m letting that read-only scan finish before narrowing into the export path.

This is a **bounded** change: the export flow and disk cache already exist; no new subsystem or public schema is required.

Verified facts:

- `src/cache.js` accepts cached rows for six hours solely from `writtenAt`; it never compares them with `data/orders.json`.
- `src/store.js` says the upstream job rewrites `data/orders.json` about every 15 minutes.
- `README.md` says ad hoc users may need freshness, while the ~400-run nightly batch needs caching to stay under ten minutes and tolerates day-old data.
- `test/exporter.test.js` protects the exact CSV order `id,placedAt,total,status`; there are no cache-freshness tests.

**Inference:** the reported symptom is caused by valid six-hour cache entries surviving newer source data. The unresolved product decision is which runs must observe a newer source; that answer determines whether we can keep one CLI contract or need a mode, and unlocks the exact concurrent-update and failure behavior questions.

questions.question: When `data/orders.json` is newer than a matching cached export, what should `reportkit` do? A wrong choice either preserves visibly stale ad hoc exports or risks the nightly runtime; current behavior uses only a six-hour cache TTL (`src/cache.js`), while both run types share the same CLI (`src/cli.js`).

options.label: Refresh on change (Recommended)
options.description: Invalidate that cached range whenever the source file is newer, keeping reuse between syncs; limitation: the first export after each rewrite pays a rebuild.

options.label: Always read source
options.description: Every export sees the current file; limitation: removes the disk-cache benefit needed by the nightly batch.

options.label: Add fresh mode
options.description: Keep current caching by default and add an explicit fresh option for ad hoc runs; limitation: users can still get stale data when they omit it.

leadIn:
Your choice establishes an explicit fresh path while preserving the nightly default.

Verified facts:

- `src/cli.js` currently accepts exactly two positional dates and has no option parser.
- `src/exporter.js` writes every computed result back to the same range cache.
- `src/store.js` performs one synchronous read and immediate JSON parse; an upstream rewrite can therefore overlap a fresh run.
- The repository contains no other writer, lock, retry policy, or stale-data warning.

**Open tension:** “fresh” still needs three observable meanings: how users request it, whether it replaces the shared cache, and whether freshness or availability wins if the source is being rewritten. These answers determine the CLI contract, cache lifetime, and recovery tests.

questions.question: How should users request fresh data? A wrong interface makes ad hoc usage error-prone; the existing command is only `reportkit <from> <to>` (`src/cli.js`).

options.label: --fresh flag (Recommended)
options.description: Use `reportkit --fresh <from> <to>` with an explicit, discoverable CLI contract; limitation: callers must change their invocation.

options.label: Environment variable
options.description: Use a process setting such as `REPORTKIT_FRESH=1`; limitation: it is less visible and easier to inherit accidentally.

questions.question: After a successful fresh export, should its rows replace the matching disk cache? A wrong answer can either leave later default runs stale or unexpectedly alter their snapshot; current computed exports always write the shared cache (`src/exporter.js`).

options.label: Replace cache (Recommended)
options.description: Later default runs reuse the newly loaded rows and avoid duplicate work; limitation: fresh ad hoc runs advance the shared nightly snapshot.

options.label: Bypass cache
options.description: Fresh output neither reads nor changes the shared cache; limitation: later default runs may still return the older cached rows.

questions.question: If fresh mode finds `data/orders.json` missing, unreadable, or malformed during a rewrite, what should users receive? A wrong answer trades correctness against availability; `loadOrders()` currently throws and the CLI exits with the runtime error (`src/store.js`).

options.label: Fail clearly (Recommended)
options.description: Exit nonzero without CSV or cache changes so `--fresh` never silently serves stale rows; limitation: users must retry after a transient rewrite.

options.label: Use stale cache
options.description: Return cached rows when available despite `--fresh`; limitation: the command can succeed with exactly the stale data it was asked to avoid.

options.label: Retry then fail
options.description: Retry the source briefly before exiting nonzero; limitation: adds latency and still cannot guarantee the rewrite duration.

leadIn:
The contract now has `--fresh`, cache bypass, and retry-on-source-failure.

Verified facts:

- Because file access is synchronous (`readFileSync` in `src/store.js`), an export computes from one successfully parsed snapshot; JavaScript code cannot interleave a second read inside it.
- A retry policy introduces new observable latency and must be bounded; the repository has no existing timing constant or convention.
- `--fresh` will neither read nor write `.reportkit-cache`, per your answer, so a failed fresh run cannot damage or rescue itself from cached state.
- The only identified concurrent writer is the upstream sync job described in `README.md`; no local command writes `data/orders.json`.

**Open tension:** we need the retry budget and the definition of “fresh” when a valid newer rewrite lands just after the successful read. These determine latency and whether the command needs stabilization/rechecking.

questions.question: How long should fresh mode retry a missing, unreadable, or malformed source before failing? A wrong budget either misses brief rewrites or makes ad hoc failures feel hung; there is no repository timing convention.

options.label: 3 tries, 100ms (Recommended)
options.description: Make three total attempts with 100 ms gaps, covering short replacement windows; limitation: only waits about 200 ms before failing.

options.label: 5 tries, 250ms
options.description: Make five total attempts with 250 ms gaps, covering longer rewrites; limitation: delays a definitive error by about one second.

options.label: 2 tries, 50ms
options.description: Make two total attempts with one 50 ms gap; limitation: is unlikely to bridge slower non-atomic rewrites.

questions.question: If a valid newer `orders.json` lands after fresh mode has successfully read its snapshot but before output completes, what should this run do? A wrong choice changes whether `--fresh` means latest at start or latest at finish; the current synchronous flow uses one snapshot (`src/store.js`, `src/exporter.js`).

options.label: Finish snapshot (Recommended)
options.description: Emit the valid snapshot read by this invocation; limitation: an update landing moments later waits for the next run.

options.label: Restart on change
options.description: Detect a changed source and recompute before output; limitation: adds file metadata checks and can repeatedly restart under frequent writes.

leadIn:
The freshness semantics are now settled: five total attempts separated by 250 ms, then use the first valid snapshot and finish from it.

Verified facts:

- The current CLI has no error handling, so read/parse failures surface as Node stack traces (`src/cli.js` calling `exportOrders` directly).
- Missing dates produce a one-line usage message and exit code 1 (`src/cli.js`).
- CSV is assembled fully before one `stdout.write`, so a source failure cannot leave a partial CSV (`src/cli.js`, `src/exporter.js`).
- Existing date strings are passed through unchanged and compared lexically; this change does not need to alter that established input contract (`src/store.js`).

**Open tension:** the final externally visible recovery detail is whether exhausted retries retain the current diagnostic stack or become a stable CLI error. This controls the failure assertion and scripting ergonomics; all other probe classes are closed by your choices, repository behavior, or inability to arise.

questions.question: After all five fresh-source attempts fail, what should stderr contain? A wrong choice either hides debugging detail or leaves an unstable stack trace for CLI callers; current failures are uncaught (`src/cli.js`).

options.label: Concise cause (Recommended)
options.description: Print one stable `reportkit:` error including the final cause and exit nonzero; limitation: omits the stack trace.

options.label: Node stack trace
options.description: Preserve the uncaught exception and full debugging context; limitation: output is noisy and unstable for scripts.

leadIn:
All 18 ledger probes are now closed. User-set closures are:

- Scope exclusion — automatic freshness for default/nightly runs: excluded by choosing **Add fresh mode**.
- Seam placement — request mechanism: **`reportkit --fresh <from> <to>`**.
- State read/write — fresh cache behavior: **bypass cache**, reading and writing neither cache state.
- Failed input — missing, unreadable, or malformed `data/orders.json`: **five total tries with 250 ms gaps**, then fail.
- Concurrent valid rewrite — a newer valid file arriving after the successful read: **finish the snapshot already read**.
- Failure UX — exhausted retries: **one concise `reportkit:` message with the final cause and nonzero exit**.

Repository closures preserve the exact CSV columns (`test/exporter.test.js`), the unchanged default six-hour cache (`src/cache.js`), single-write output that prevents partial CSV (`src/cli.js`), and existing lexical range filtering (`src/store.js`). Duplicate and repeated fresh calls are read-only and independent; no repository writer other than the documented upstream sync exists (`README.md`).

**Resolved contract:** add opt-in `--fresh`; successful fresh runs load a valid current snapshot without touching cache; transient source failures retry as specified; default runs and CSV shape remain unchanged. Explicitly excluded: automatic cache invalidation, date-validation changes, cache-format changes, and dependency additions. The proving check will run `node --test` with focused CLI/export tests for fresh bypass, retry success/exhaustion, concise failure, default cache preservation, and CSV order.

**Inference / dependency map:** this is implementation-ready if the contract is correct; confirmation unlocks code and tests, while any correction reopens only the affected ledger probes.

questions.question: Is this resolved contract complete and correct before implementation begins? The implementation and acceptance tests will follow it exactly.

options.label: Implement it (Recommended)
options.description: Proceed with the settled contract; limitation: automatic freshness remains intentionally out of scope.

options.label: Revise contract
options.description: Pause implementation and reopen the affected decisions; limitation: no code changes will be made until the correction is settled.
